_comment: Curated SSC-CGL / UPSC editorial vocabulary bank. Offline fallback source. Each entry: word, pos (part of speech), meaning (simple), easy (easy synonyms), example (newspaper-style sentence). Add more entries any time; the generator dedupes against words already used.

words.meaning: to say someone did something wrong, without proof yet
words.example: The report alleges that the company hid its losses.
The government announced new rules to curb pollution in the city.

words.meaning: a big fall or weak period
words.example: The economy is facing a slump as factories cut production.
A probe has been ordered into the bridge collapse.
Leaders hailed the agreement as a historic step.
The opposition slammed the budget for ignoring farmers.
The minister vowed to complete the project by next year.
Stock markets plunged amid global tension.

words.meaning: to make something less harmful or severe
words.example: New flood barriers were built to mitigate the damage from storms.

words.meaning: to make a bad situation worse
words.example: Cutting subsidies could exacerbate the crisis for poor families.
Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.

words.meaning: to fall very fast and far
words.example: Exports plummeted after the new tariffs were imposed.

words.meaning: able to recover quickly from difficulty
words.example: The economy proved resilient despite the pandemic shock.

words.meaning: to shock or excite someone into action
words.example: The disaster galvanised the public into demanding reform.

words.meaning: strict economic policy with reduced spending
words.example: Years of austerity led to widespread protests across the country.

words.meaning: a group of parties or people working together
words.example: A fragile coalition government took power after the election.

words.meaning: a penalty against a country, or official permission
words.example: The nation faced harsh sanctions over its nuclear programme.

words.meaning: a situation where no side can win or move forward
words.example: Talks ended in a stalemate, with neither side willing to compromise.

words.meaning: to formally approve an agreement or treaty
words.example: Parliament voted to ratify the climate treaty.
The bank cut rates to bolster the slowing economy.
The deal came under intense scrutiny from regulators.

words.meaning: dealing with things practically, not idealistically
words.example: The leader took a pragmatic approach to the trade dispute.
The contentious bill divided lawmakers sharply.
The country faced an unprecedented heatwave this summer.
Relations between the two nations continued to deteriorate.

words.meaning: to publicly support a cause; a supporter
words.example: She advocates for stronger laws against child labour.
Forecasters warned of an imminent cyclone along the coast.

words.meaning: a return or rise after a decline
words.example: The region saw a resurgence of the virus in winter.
The campaign was full of fiery rhetoric but few real plans.

words.meaning: likely to change suddenly and unpredictably
words.example: Oil prices remained volatile amid the conflict.
Members failed to reach a consensus on the new policy.
Several economists endorsed the reform package.

words.meaning: producing a lot of money or profit
words.example: The firm won a lucrative contract to build the highway.

words.meaning: to become or make smaller or less
words.example: Public trust in the institution has steadily diminished.
Some job losses were inevitable after the merger.

words.meaning: a state of great confusion or disorder
words.example: The country was plunged into political turmoil.

words.meaning: something that causes change or action
words.example: The protest became a catalyst for nationwide reform.
The agency imposed stringent safety standards on factories.
Public support for the war began to wane.

words.meaning: to slow down or get in the way of progress
words.example: Heavy rain hampered rescue operations.

words.meaning: to say something again for emphasis
words.example: The minister reiterated the need for unity.
An inadvertent error delayed the entire project.

words.meaning: weak, thin, or not strongly supported
words.example: The link between the two events is tenuous at best.
Fake news proliferated during the election.

words.meaning: official order or authority to act
words.example: The new government claimed a strong mandate from voters.
The report painted a bleak picture of the job market.
There was a surge in demand for electric cars.
The lockdown curtailed many basic freedoms.
The onus is on the company to prove its product is safe.
Millions live in precarious financial conditions.

words.meaning: to prove someone right or free from blame
words.example: The verdict vindicated the whistle-blower.

words.meaning: to stop or suppress something, often by force
words.example: Police were called in to quell the riots.
There is a wide disparity between rich and poor regions.

words.meaning: to encourage the growth of something
words.example: The scheme aims to foster innovation among startups.
The government offered a belated apology to the victims.

words.meaning: a temporary relief from trouble or punishment
words.example: Falling prices gave consumers a brief reprieve.
The data revealed a stark rise in unemployment.
Investors remained wary of the new market.
Authorities struggled to subdue the spreading unrest.

words.meaning: the situation after a bad event
words.example: Thousands were left homeless in the aftermath of the flood.
The lawyer made a compelling case for reform.

words.meaning: to gradually wear away or weaken
words.example: Corruption has eroded faith in public institutions.
Businesses are worried about a looming recession.
The city faces an acute shortage of drinking water.

words.meaning: to state a clear condition in an agreement
words.example: The contract stipulates a strict deadline.

words.meaning: the main force or worst part of something
words.example: Poor families bore the brunt of the price rise.
Aid groups implored the world to send help.

words.meaning: to slowly shrink or run low
words.example: Water supplies dwindled during the long drought.
The offer was spurned by union leaders.

words.meaning: something that is different from normal
words.example: Scientists noticed an anomaly in the climate data.

words.meaning: the state of sticking together or unity
words.example: The crisis tested the cohesion of the alliance.
Red tape continues to impede small businesses.
There was a brief lull in the fighting.

words.meaning: real and able to be clearly seen or felt
words.example: The talks produced no tangible results.
Critics called the deal lopsided and unfair.

words.meaning: to give someone courage to act
words.example: The win emboldened the protesters to demand more.

words.meaning: done with great care and effort
words.example: Restoring the temple took painstaking work.

words.meaning: to think or consider; to deal with
words.example: Analysts reckon growth will slow next year.
She raised several pertinent questions in the debate.
Political disputes stymied the relief effort.

words.meaning: existing but not yet visible or active
words.example: The policy exposed latent tensions in society.

words.meaning: to reach a final or highest point
words.example: Months of protests culminated in a mass strike.
She is adept at handling difficult negotiations.
The country squandered its oil wealth on vanity projects.

words.meaning: a thin, often false, outer appearance
words.example: Behind the veneer of calm lay deep anxiety.
The strike crippled public transport for days.
A few recalcitrant states blocked the reform.
The nascent industry needs government support.
A deft handling of the crisis won her praise.

words.meaning: to lose a right or possession as a penalty
words.example: Defaulters may forfeit their deposits.
Violence marred the otherwise peaceful rally.
The decision had serious economic repercussions.
The plan met with a tepid response from voters.

words.meaning: to express sorrow or complaint about
words.example: Farmers bemoaned the lack of fair prices.

words.meaning: to give up power or territory
words.example: The party refused to cede control of the council.
The response to the disaster was widely called inept.

words.meaning: a thorough change or repair of a system
words.example: The tax system is due for a major overhaul.
The brazen theft happened in broad daylight.

words.meaning: to dry up, fade, or weaken
words.example: Support for the scheme withered within months.
The press lambasted the government for inaction.

words.meaning: to restore friendly relations; to make agree
words.example: It is hard to reconcile growth with environmental care.
His position became untenable after the scandal.

words.meaning: a difficult situation hard to escape
words.example: The war turned into a costly quagmire.
The editor summarised the salient points of the report.

words.meaning: to control or choke; to limit severely
words.example: New rules could throttle online free speech.
Activists demanded a more equitable sharing of resources.

words.meaning: harmful in a slow, hidden way
words.example: Misinformation has a pernicious effect on democracy.

words.meaning: to cause great harm or damage
words.example: The floods wreaked havoc across the state.
The market stayed buoyant despite the bad news.

words.meaning: to make someone lose hope or trust
words.example: Many young voters feel disenchanted with politics.

words.meaning: to build or create (a bond); to fake
words.example: The two nations forged a new trade partnership.
The sanctions inflicted heavy losses on the economy.
Wages have remained stagnant for years.

words.meaning: a long angry speech of criticism
words.example: He launched into a tirade against the media.

words.meaning: to hold and use power or a tool
words.example: The committee wields great influence over policy.
There were ominous signs of an economic slowdown.

words.meaning: to calm someone who is angry
words.example: The minister tried to placate angry protesters.
Corruption is rampant in many departments.
The deal had the tacit approval of the leadership.

words.meaning: to bring in or begin a new period
words.example: The reforms ushered in a new era of growth.
The promise was vague and lacked detail.

words.meaning: to take something by force or effort
words.example: The opposition wrested control of three states.
The policy mainly benefits affluent households.

words.meaning: slow, heavy, and hard to use
words.example: The approval process is cumbersome and slow.
Aid agencies warned of a dire humanitarian crisis.
The fledgling democracy faced many challenges.
The survivors described a grim scene of destruction.

words.meaning: large in amount, size, or weight
words.example: The court imposed a hefty fine on the firm.

words.meaning: a lack of movement or unwillingness to change
words.example: Bureaucratic inertia delayed the much-needed reform.
The leak could jeopardise national security.
There is keen interest in the new policy.

words.meaning: to remain in a bad or weak state
words.example: Thousands of cases languish in the courts for years.
Workers earn a meagre wage for long hours.

words.meaning: a small but important difference in meaning
words.example: The debate ignored the nuances of the issue.

words.meaning: not well known or hard to understand; to hide
words.example: The real cause remains obscure to investigators.
Public safety must be of paramount importance.

words.meaning: the most perfect example of something
words.example: It was a quintessential case of bureaucratic delay.
The country posted robust economic growth.
The audit was a scathing indictment of the management.

words.meaning: to prevent someone from doing something
words.example: Security forces thwarted a major attack.
False claims undermine public trust in science.
He was a vehement critic of the new law.

words.meaning: a turning point that changes everything
words.example: The verdict was a watershed moment for civil rights.
Literacy is a key yardstick of development.
Reformers pursued change with great zeal.
The storm finally began to abate by evening.

words.meaning: a cause of great trouble or ruin
words.example: Unemployment is the bane of the youth.

words.meaning: believing people act only out of self-interest
words.example: Voters have grown cynical about politicians' promises.

words.meaning: seeming difficult and scary to face
words.example: Rebuilding the city is a daunting task.

words.meaning: to support or adopt a belief
words.example: The party espouses free-market policies.
She made a fervent appeal for peace.
The survey tried to gauge public opinion.

words.meaning: a sign of something to come
words.example: Falling sales were a harbinger of recession.

words.meaning: a force that drives something forward
words.example: The crisis gave fresh impetus to reform.

words.meaning: to place side by side for comparison
words.example: The article juxtaposes wealth and poverty.

words.meaning: to start or arouse a feeling
words.example: The speech kindled hope among the people.

words.meaning: a lack of energy or enthusiasm
words.example: Economic lethargy gripped the region for years.
The reform faces a myriad of challenges.
The area is notorious for its high crime rate.

words.meaning: hard to see through or understand
words.example: The deal's terms remain opaque to the public.
Prudent spending helped the state avoid debt.

words.meaning: to calm or put an end to
words.example: Officials moved quickly to quell rumours.

words.meaning: an act of revenge or retaliation
words.example: Witnesses stayed silent for fear of reprisal.
She is a staunch supporter of the reform.
The session was truncated due to protests.

words.meaning: a big and sudden change or disturbance
words.example: The reforms caused major social upheaval.

words.meaning: to speak about someone in a very bad way
words.example: Critics were vilified in the state media.

words.meaning: deliberate and without reason or care
words.example: The report described wanton destruction of forests.

words.meaning: a person with extreme, uncompromising views
words.example: A few zealots derailed the peace talks.
